topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
consensus_response: To optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations, adaptive phased array antennas (APAs) can be employed to dynamically adjust the array factor, allowing for real-time optimization of coverage and interference. The challenge lies in making rapid and precise adjustments while balancing the trade-offs between coverage area and directivity. This requires careful consideration of satellite spacing, array factor, and service zone radius to minimize interference and maintain coverage during brief service windows.
reference_context: In LEO constellations, a communication system of 60…70 satellites equally spaced in ascending nodes of the orbit can cover the whole surface of the earth. The time of satellite flight over a subscriber can range from 10 minutes to 20 minutes, and the orbit altitude of around 900 km, the inclination of 74º, and the zone of subscriber radio visibility above the 7º local horizon correspond to the satellite service zone radius of more than 2500 km.
